QUOTE: Calls `client.createPost` again, which is one attempt. ... On failure, applies the same rules as the first send: the three error types above remove the post, and anything else sets `failed: true` again so the user can retry once more.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says that retryFailedPost makes a single new createPost attempt and, on failure, removes the post for the same three errors or marks it failed again. It also notes the HTTP layer has retryLimit 0, so there is no loop or backoff.
